summary: Weekly POC check-in for Redwood Private VPC pilot with NexaHealth. Main topics: networking/routing hiccups observed during burst tests, plan for targeted maintenance to apply quantization/kernel patches, security clarifications around KMS and audit logs, and next steps for benchmarking. Agreed next steps and owners, schedule maintenance for 2026-08-13.
transcript:
Header: 2026-08-12 17:00 UTC | Duration 45m | Attendees: Avery Chen, Samir Patel, Jules Rivera (Redwood) / Lauren Kim, Diego Rivera, Priya Singh, Evan Morris (NexaHealth)

00:00 Avery: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll kick off, quick check - is everyone seeing audio ok?
00:06 Lauren: yep good here, thanks.
00:08 Samir: audio's fine. quick agenda: routing updates, pilot perf numbers, kernel/quant tweaks, security questions, and next steps.
00:18 Diego: sounds good. we had another fail during late burst test yesterday, so would like to go through that.

02:12 Avery: quick context for folks - we've been running the Redwood Private stack in your VPC, two worker nodes on the pilot subnet, with autoscaling disabled for the test. we've observed intermittent 502/timeout when we push to 80 concurrent sessions, mostly in the 30-40 minute mark.
02:30 Lauren: exactly, the app team sees timeouts and then things sort of recover. seemed like a routing thing?
02:38 Samir: based on the logs we saw, there's a mix - some requests are getting to the inference runtime, others drop earlier at the NLB level. Could be connection tracking exhaustion on the NAT gateway or ephemeral port limits on the firewall.
03:01 Priya: we did bump the connection tracking recently but i'll double-check. also flagged that the customer-side firewall had shorter TCP timeouts.

05:15 Diego: we captured some tcpdump - there are SYN retransmits and then RSTs from the NLB, i can share raw pcap.
05:22 Avery: please do, Diego. drop it into the pilot channel. that'll help us correlate.

07:40 Samir: on the runtime side i want to call out two things: kernel selection and KV-cache pressure during long sequences. The model we loaded is the open-llm-2-13b quantized variant; with the default kernel path we saw a gradual increase in memory pressure and CPU spikes at 10-15s per request window.
07:58 Evan: is that the quantized path you suggested earlier? we did a quick switch but maybe not the latest patch.
08:05 Samir: right, we rolled quantization but there's a recent patch that improves fused attention kernels for that model. I'll push that to the pilot nodes in the maintenance window. should shave off about 10-15% latency on long sequences.

10:32 Lauren: what's the expected downtime for that patch? we can't interrupt core workflows during PST business hours.
10:38 Samir: short rolling restarts per node, we estimate 10-12 minutes per node; if we do a staged restart and drain connections it's low risk. propose maintenance 2026-08-13 02:00 UTC to minimize impact.
10:52 Lauren: that works for us, i'll confirm with infra team, but please send invite.

12:00 Priya: on security, quick Q: for the pilot you're using our KMS to wrap model keys? and audit logs are streaming to our SIEM?
12:10 Avery: yes for Private we support customer-managed KMS and we configured the pilot to use your KMS key. audit logs are delivered to the configured CloudWatch log group and we can forward to your SIEM.
12:22 Priya: i saw some earlier logs that looked like partial entries, are we retaining full request/response or truncating? compliance needs full request IDs but we redact payloads.
12:34 Jules: right now we retain metadata, request IDs, latency, token counts. payloads are redacted by default. if you need expanded retention or a custom retention policy we can enable, but need sign-off for storage costs.

15:05 Diego: back to networking, the pattern shows failures matching NAT gateway CPU bump and then connection table overflow. We have a ticket to increase scaling but we need guidance if changing timeouts on firewall is safe.
15:20 Samir: two levers: increase conntrack table sizes and tweak idle timeouts, or use a proxy layer (we can add a connection pooling LB inside the VPC). We recommended the conntrack increase as low-effort.
15:37 Lauren: are there security implications to increasing conntrack? Priya?
15:42 Priya: it's fine but need to document and ensure it doesn't exceed audit thresholds; i'll put it on my checklist.

18:00 Evan: performance numbers from last run - p99 latency was 1.9s for short convo, but long-sequence p95 jumped to 8.4s and we saw 5 timeouts. baseline expected p95 < 3s.
18:18 Samir: after the kernel patch and enabling more aggressive KV caching we expect long-sequence p95 to drop under 4s, maybe lower. also need to tune batching: your workload is spiky with lots of small requests mixed with a few long ones. smart routing to a cheaper model variant for short requests could reduce load.
18:40 Lauren: how hard is to route short vs long? can we do header-based routing?
18:46 Samir: yes, we can add a lightweight classifier in the edge to route based on expected tokens. it's a config change and we can prototype it in a day.

22:05 Diego: SIG: we had one session where the model failed to fall back to smaller variant when the GPU was saturated - it kept queuing. is that a Redwood timeout setting?
22:18 Avery: good find - the pilot had fallback policies set to none to make behavior deterministic. we can enable automatic fallback to the 7B-compatible variant when queue length > threshold. I'll update the rollout policy.
22:30 Lauren: prefer automatic fallback so customer-facing services don't see errors.

26:00 Priya: quick on compliance - do you have our requested SSO metadata and SCIM provisioning test results?
26:08 Jules: sent yesterday; you should have the SAML metadata in the pilot doc. if anything missing i'll re-send.
26:15 Priya: ok saw that, thanks. on SOC2 we need encryption-at-rest proof for model cache and we need audit trail for any key rotations.
26:28 Avery: we'll provide the encryption config and rotation policy screenshots; Samir will include the config path.

30:40 Samir: maintenance plan recap: push fused attention kernel + quant patch, enable KV-cache aggressive heuristics, enable fallback policy, drain nodes in rolling restart. Target 2026-08-13 02:00 UTC.
30:55 Diego: on our side we'll increase conntrack and monitor, and capture tcpdump during the next stress run.
31:05 Lauren: i will coordinate with oncall to accept maintenance window.

35:12 Evan: question - any expected change in monthly cost if we enable longer retention of logs and additional metrics?
35:20 Jules: yes more retention increases storage costs; we gave an estimate in the bench spreadsheet. Avery will attach updated cost breakdown after the maintenance.
35:30 Avery: yep i'll upload updated bench numbers and a cost delta.

38:50 Priya: final thing - KMS: can Redwood support HSM-backed keys? our compliance team prefers it.
38:58 Avery: yes, we integrate with customer HSM via cloud KMS providers that expose HSM-backed keys. we'll send reference architecture and the required IAM role bindings.
39:12 Priya: great, please send that to priya@nexahealth.com.

42:00 Avery: ok recap of next steps: we'll share updated VPC routing diagram and maintenance invite; Samir will push patch during the window; Diego will run stress bench and share tcpdump; Priya to confirm KMS/HSM requirements; and Avery to update bench/cost sheet.
42:23 Lauren: sounds good, thanks everyone.
42:30 Avery: thanks all, we'll follow up in the pilot channel and I'll send notes + links.
42:37 Jules: thanks, bye.
42:40 Meeting end.
